units.text: Assertions are used to verify that the elements exist or have certain attributes.

quotes.quote: Assertions are used to verify that the elements exist or have certain attributes.

units.text: Check assertions by calling `assert()` on the `SemanticsNodeInteraction` returned by a finder with one or multiple matchers:

quotes.quote: Check assertions by calling assert() on the SemanticsNodeInteraction returned by a finder with one or multiple matchers:

units.text:
// Single matcher:
composeTestRule
    .onNode(matcher)
    .assert(hasText("Button")) // hasText is a SemanticsMatcher

// Multiple matchers can use and / or
composeTestRule
    .onNode(matcher).assert(hasText("Button") or hasText("Button2"))

units.text: Actions inject simulated user events on the elements, such as clicks or other gestures.

quotes.quote: Actions inject simulated user events on the elements, such as clicks or other gestures.

units.text: To inject an action on a node, call a `perform...()` function:

quotes.quote: To inject an action on a node, call a perform...() function:

units.text: composeTestRule.onNode(...).performClick()

quotes.quote: composeTestRule.onNode(...).performClick()

units.text: You cannot chain actions inside a perform function. Instead, make multiple `perform...()` calls.

quotes.quote: You cannot chain actions inside a perform function. Instead, make multiple perform...() calls.

units.text: - `performClick` performs a click action on the element represented by the given semantics node. Depending on the platform this may be implemented by a touch click (tap), a mouse click, or another more appropriate method for that platform.

quotes.quote: Performs a click action on the element represented by the given semantics node. Depending on the platform this may be implemented by a touch click (tap), a mouse click, or another more appropriate method for that platform.

units.text: - `performSemanticsAction(key)` provides support to call custom semantics actions on this node. This method is for calling actions that have no parameters. It throws `AssertionError` if the semantics action is not defined on this node.

quotes.quote: Provides support to call custom semantics actions on this node.
This method is for calling actions that have no parameters.
If the semantics action is not defined on this node.

units.text: - `performKeyPress(keyEvent)` sends the specified `KeyEvent` to the focused component. It returns true if the event was consumed and false otherwise.

@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4::class) class FocusNavigationTest { @get:Rule val composeTestRule = createComposeRule()

units.text: You can verify whether a UI element can receive focus by performing a click or requesting focus, and then asserting its state using `assertIsFocused()` and `assertIsNotFocused()`.

quotes.quote: You can verify whether a UI element can receive focus by performing a click or requesting focus, and then asserting its state using

@Test fun interactiveElement_isFocusTarget() { composeTestRule.setContent { AppTheme { CardListScreen() } } val firstCard = composeTestRule.onNodeWithTag("card_1") val secondCard = composeTestRule.onNodeWithTag("card_2") // Focus the first element firstCard.performClick() firstCard.assertIsFocused() secondCard.assertIsNotFocused() }

units.text: As a best practice, verify both forward navigation (`Key.Tab`) and reverse navigation (`Key.Tab` with `Key.ShiftLeft` held down) to ensure two-way traversal integrity:

quotes.quote: As a best practice, verify both forward navigation (Key.Tab) and reverse navigation (Key.Tab with Key.ShiftLeft held down) to ensure two-way traversal integrity:

@Test fun tabKey_navigatesInAppearanceOrder() { composeTestRule.setContent { AppTheme { CardListScreen() } } val firstCard = composeTestRule.onNodeWithTag("card_1") val secondCard = composeTestRule.onNodeWithTag("card_2") val thirdCard = composeTestRule.onNodeWithTag("card_3") firstCard.performClick() firstCard.assertIsFocused() // Press Tab -> Moves to second card firstCard.performKeyInput { pressKey(Key.Tab) } secondCard.assertIsFocused() firstCard.assertIsNotFocused() // Press Tab -> Moves to third card secondCard.performKeyInput { pressKey(Key.Tab) } thirdCard.assertIsFocused() // Press Shift + Tab -> Moves backward to second card thirdCard.performKeyInput { withKeyDown(Key.ShiftLeft) { pressKey(Key.Tab) } } secondCard.assertIsFocused() }

units.text: When migrating to the v2 APIs, tests can fail if they rely on non-touch input modes configured through instrumentation APIs before the test starts. Within the setup functions for tests, the system enforces `InputMode.Touch` by default at the start of each test for more determinism and to prevent state leakage, overriding ambient device state and pre-test setup.
